subject: POC trial: model selection & success criteria

Subject: POC trial: model selection & success criteria

Thanks for the time today, Anna - great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get the POC scoped and scheduled.

High-level goal
- Validate model quality and latency for Acme Retail's multilingual customer support use case (English + Spanish + French).

Success criteria (what Acme wants to see during the trial)
- Accuracy/Quality: intent classification + reply generation quality meets your acceptance threshold on our QA prompts (target: > 92% intent accuracy on the eval set).
- Latency: 95th percentile inference latency under 300ms for single-turn responses at your typical payload (avg 128 tokens).
- Cost: per-conversation inference cost estimate within your budget target (we'll provide cost/1K token numbers).
- Reliability: automatic fallback to secondary model if primary model latency or errors spike.

Evaluation plan
1) Week 0 (prep): exchange test dataset schema and secure access (S3 link or shared Drive).
2) Week 1: deploy trial models in Redwood Dedicated sandbox, run regression/eval suite on your sample data.
3) Week 2: run live traffic shadow tests (sample of production traffic you send), collect metrics and qualitative examples.
4) Week 3: review results, adjust model/config (quantization/profile/batching) and agree on next steps (pilot or rollout).

Timeline
- Proposed POC kickoff: week of Oct 12 (3-week engagement).

Ownership
- Acme: Anna Jensen (product) + Liam Ortiz (engineering) - provide dataset, prod sample traffic, and whitelisting details.
- Redwood: Marissa Cole (commercial lead), Aditya Rao (technical lead), Connor O'Brien (customer success).

Immediate next steps
- Can you confirm the kickoff week of Oct 12 and share a link to a representative dataset (or let us know S3/Drive access)?
- We'll send a short onboarding checklist and a proposed POC plan PDF (attached).

Thanks - looking forward to getting this running.

Best,
Marissa
Head of Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference

Anna - great, thanks for confirming. Below is the Redwood recommendation for the trial model set and a slightly more detailed evaluation checklist.

Proposed model selection (trial)
- Primary model (quality + multilingual): Llama-2-70b-chat (4-bit quantized profile) - selected for strong multilingual capabilities and high-quality generation on customer-support prompts.
- Fallback model (fast + cheap): Mistral-7b-instruct (4-bit quantized) - lower latency/cost profile for heavy traffic and as an automatic failover if the primary exceeds latency/error thresholds.

Why this combo
- Llama-2-70b-chat gives us strong few-shot and instruction-following quality for English/Spanish; quantization keeps cost manageable.
- Mistral-7b is smaller and tends to have faster per-token throughput, making it a good fallback for degraded conditions.

Evaluation checklist (what Redwood will measure during POC)
- Quantitative: intent accuracy, response correctness (manual labels on a 200-sample eval set), BLEU/ROUGE where applicable, 95p latency, error rate (5000 requests sample), and cost estimate per 1K tokens.
- Qualitative: 20 curated customer example threads reviewed by your product team; hallucination cases flagged and triaged.
- Operational: autoscaling/throughput at expected concurrency, model cold-start behavior, and fallback behavior correctness.

Deliverables
- Weekly metrics dashboard (latency/cost/quality).
- Shared eval report at end of week 3 with pass/fail against agreed success criteria.

Attachments: redwood_model_profiles.pdf (model perf/expected latency matrix)

If that looks good, we'll:
- Lock models and schedule a technical kickoff (Aditya to lead).
- Share SOC2 checklist and evidence pack (Connor will coordinate).

Marissa

Hi Anna / team - quick technical notes ahead of the kickoff next week. Copying Connor for Ops & SOC coordination.

- Whitelist / networking: please provide the IP ranges we'll need to allow (or the SAML metadata if you're using SSO). We will provide a temporary sandbox endpoint.
- Dataset: thanks for the Drive link - we'll run our preprocessing script to verify tokenization and label format. Typical POC dataset size we use for the eval run is 1.5k-5k anonymized examples; let us know if you want us to subsample.
- Tokenization & multilingual: Llama-2 tokenizers handle Spanish well; for French we recommend adding a few dozen curated examples to the eval set to validate edge cases (accented characters, contractions).
- Quantization caveats: 4-bit quant is what we'll use initially to reduce cost. We'll test accuracy delta vs fp16 on a small sample and flag regressions. If a specific prompt family degrades >4 points, we'll propose a targeted fp16 run for that family.
- Fallback behavior: we'll implement automatic routing by SLO (95p latency > 300ms OR error rate > 2%) to Mistral-7b. We'll include logs for each failover event in the dashboard.

Links: POC artifacts (shared Drive) - https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c4d5e6f
CRM: HubSpot record HS-43892

I'll upload a short onboarding checklist and a runbook for how we enable fallback routing to the Drive folder today.
